result.title: Keep Images in Sight: Visual Position Re-Anchoring for Long-Context MLLMs
result.summary: Long-context multimodal intelligence requires revisiting earlier images as conversations and documents accumulate, yet retaining an image does not guarantee reliable access to its details. By varying context length, redistributing a fixed text passage around the image, and changing positions without adding text, we identify the positional relation between images and questions as a direct influence on visual access. To address this gap, we propose Visual Position Re-Anchoring (VPR), a training-free method that shifts cached visual-key rotary phases toward a short-context reference before question processing. It operates directly on the existing KV cache, preserving standard attention computation without extracting attention maps or adding model forward passes. We develop static and continuous compensation schedules, using the static schedule by default. Across ten checkpoints and ten benchmarks, static VPR improves 97 of 100 model--task scores. Further analysis shows greater attention to regions containing answer evidence across six checkpoints, with minimal runtime overhead under fixed rotary frequencies. These findings demonstrate an efficient way to sustain visual access through positional adjustment within the cache.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究长上下文 MLLM 中图像与问题的位置关系如何影响视觉信息访问，提出免训练的 Visual Position Re-Anchoring：在现有 KV cache 上把视觉键的旋转相位调向短上下文参照，并提供静态与连续补偿方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对位置、KV cache 与注意力结构影响视觉证据访问的诊断，直接关联 LVR 中的视觉细节保留、证据筛选及 latent 相似度受位置与缓存结构影响的问题；可供核查相位重锚能否改善推理期的视觉证据使用。
